chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is written in the Torah: 'Thank the one who bestows favor upon you, and bestow favor upon the one who thanks you, for there is no decline of the bounties when they are thanked for, and there is no permanence for them when they are denied. Gratitude is an increase in the bounties and a safety from changes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of gratitude according to the Torah as cited in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'Shukr al-Ni'ma' (gratitude for blessings) by citing a verse from the Torah, illustrating the Shia tradition of drawing wisdom from previous scriptures. It establishes that gratitude serves as both a mechanism for increasing divine favor and a safeguard against sudden changes in fortune, while ingratitude inevitably leads to the loss of blessings.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Baghdady, from Abdullah Bin Is’haq Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It is written in the Torah: “Thank the one who favours upon you, and do favours upon the one who thanks you, for there would be no decline of the Bounties when it is thanked for, and there would not remain when it is denied. The gratefulness increases in the Bounties, and it is a safety from the changes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ishaq al-Ja’fari from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘This is written in the Torah: “Thank (and be grateful to) those who have done favors to you, and do favors to those who thank you; bounties will not go away if you appreciate them and they will not stay all the time if you reject them. Thankfulness increases the bounties and provides security against changes (from good to worse).””’
